newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua port says meetings over strike continue.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua port says meetings over strike continue.

text.p: The key Brazilian port of Paranagua was operating on a work-to-rule basis as dockworkers and port operators met to hammer out a last-minute deal to avert a strike, the port authority said.
"They are meeting at the moment, the dockworkers, the port operators and the superintendent who is acting as a mediator," said a spokeswoman for the port.
"The superintendent agrees with the port operators' position as all the other workers have already received this salary increase," she said.
All port operations have been reduced to a minimum, except for loadings of soybeans, soymeal and corn in the export corridor, which was not expected to be affected by the strike.
Port operators and dockworkers on Tuesday announced they were unable to agree on the dockworkers' demand for a 21 percent pay increase and a 72-hour strike would begin at 1200 GMT.
Dockworkers said they were still open to negotiations and would call off the strike if they were awarded the pay rise immediately.

Port authorities declined to confirm a report that the strike would cost Paranagua port 1.5 million reais ($1.43 million) per day. "There is no such calculation. The cost has not been measured," the spokeswoman said.
She added there was currently a 15-km queue of trucks waiting to unload soybeans and soymeal at the port, but this was normal as the Brazilian soybean harvest gets into full swing.
The trucks would continue to unload their cargoes even during a strike because they were unloading in privately-owned warehouses and at the export terminal, she said.
